at opdage.explanation: "At opdage" means "to discover", finding or noticing something you did not know about: Jeg opdagede en fejl (I noticed a mistake). It often comes as a surprise: Hun opdagede, at tasken var væk (She discovered that the bag was gone).

sentence.da: Vi vil gerne **opdage** nye steder på rejsen.
sentence.en: We would like to discover new places on the trip.

at opdatere.explanation: "At opdatere" means "to update", to make something new or current, like a program or a list: Hun opdaterer listen hver uge (She updates the list every week).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **opdatere** min telefon i aften.
sentence.en: I want to update my phone tonight.

at operere.explanation: "At operere" means "to operate", on a patient: Lægen opererer i morgen (The doctor operates tomorrow). It is also used for a business working somewhere: Firmaet opererer i Europa (The company operates in Europe).

sentence.da: Lægen skal **operere** min mor i morgen.
sentence.en: The doctor is going to operate on my mother tomorrow.

at opføre sig.explanation: "At opføre sig" means "to behave", and it needs a word like pænt (nicely) or dårligt (badly): Han opfører sig dårligt (He behaves badly). Without sig, at opføre means "to build": De opfører et hus (They are building a house).

sentence.da: Børn skal **opføre sig** pænt i skolen.
sentence.en: Children must behave nicely at school.

at oplade.explanation: "At oplade" means "to charge", to fill a battery with power: Jeg oplader min computer (I charge my computer). In daily speech, at lade (to charge) is just as common.

sentence.da: Jeg skal **oplade** min telefon i nat.
sentence.en: I have to charge my phone tonight.

at opleve.explanation: "At opleve" means "to experience", for things you see or that happen to you: Vi oplevede en flot solopgang (We saw a beautiful sunrise). It is often used for trips and events: Jeg oplevede en koncert i Berlin (I got to see a concert in Berlin).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **opleve** Italien en dag.
sentence.en: I would like to experience Italy one day.

at optage.explanation: "At optage" means "to record" sound or video: Jeg optager sangen (I am recording the song). It also means "to take up" room: Det optager meget plads (It takes up a lot of space).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **optage** sangen på min telefon.
sentence.en: I would like to record the song on my phone.

at ordne.explanation: "At ordne" means "to fix" or "to sort out" a task or problem: Jeg ordner det (I will sort it out). Jeg skal ordne nogle ting (I have to take care of some things).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **ordne** papirerne til banken.
sentence.en: I have to sort out the papers for the bank.

at organisere.explanation: "At organisere" means "to organize", planning and arranging something: Hun organiserer en tur (She is organizing a trip). It can also mean putting things in order: Jeg organiserer mine filer (I am organizing my files).

sentence.da: Vi vil **organisere** en stor fest for hende.
sentence.en: We want to organize a big party for her.

at orke.explanation: "At orke" means "to have the energy for", and it is mostly used in questions and with ikke (not): Jeg orker ikke mere (I can't take any more). Orker du at gå en tur? (Do you have the energy for a walk?)

forms.en: I have had the energy for

sentence.da: Jeg er træt og kan ikke **orke** at lave mad.
sentence.en: I am tired and cannot face cooking.

at overføre penge.explanation: "At overføre penge" means "to transfer money", for example from one account to another: Hun overfører penge hver måned (She transfers money every month). You can also say at sende penge (to send money).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **overføre penge** til dig i aften.
sentence.en: I can transfer money to you tonight.

at overhale.explanation: "At overhale" means "to overtake", to pass a car or a bike on the road: Hun overhaler en traktor (She overtakes a tractor). To catch up with someone ahead of you, use at indhente (to catch up): Jeg indhenter dig (I catch up with you).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **overhale** den langsomme bil foran os.
sentence.en: I want to overtake the slow car in front of us.

at overleve.explanation: "At overleve" means "to survive": Han overlevede ulykken (He survived the accident). It is built from over (over) and leve (to live), so it means to live through something.

sentence.da: Man kan ikke **overleve** uden vand.
sentence.en: You cannot survive without water.

at overnatte.explanation: "At overnatte" means "to stay overnight", for example at a hotel, a hostel or a friend's house. Vi overnatter på hotel means "We stay the night at a hotel".

sentence.da: Vi vil **overnatte** på et hotel.
sentence.en: We want to stay overnight at a hotel.

at overraske.explanation: "At overraske" means "to surprise": Jeg vil overraske min mor (I want to surprise my mom). It also means to catch someone off guard: Regnen overraskede os (The rain surprised us).

sentence.da: Han vil **overraske** sin kone med en rejse.
sentence.en: He wants to surprise his wife with a trip.

at oversætte.explanation: "At oversætte" means "to translate": Jeg oversætter brevet (I translate the letter). Use fra (from) and til (to) for the languages: Hun oversætter fra dansk til tysk (She translates from Danish to German).

sentence.da: Kan du **oversætte** det her til engelsk?
sentence.en: Can you translate this into English?

at overtale.explanation: "At overtale" means "to persuade", getting someone to say yes: Hun overtalte mig til at komme med (She persuaded me to come along). Use til at (to) before the action.

sentence.da: Hun vil **overtale** sin chef til at give hende fri.
sentence.en: She wants to persuade her boss to give her time off.

at overveje.explanation: "At overveje" means "to consider", which is thinking about something carefully before you decide: Jeg overvejer at flytte (I am considering moving). A quick thought is different: Jeg tænker på mad (I am thinking about food).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **overveje** tilbuddet i et par dage.
sentence.en: I will consider the offer for a couple of days.

en offside.explanation: "En offside" means "an offside", when a player is too far ahead of the others when the ball is passed: Dommeren fløjtede for offside (The referee blew the whistle for offside).

sentence.da: Der var **offside**, så målet tæller ikke.
sentence.en: It was offside, so the goal does not count.

en oldefar.explanation: "En oldefar" means "a great-grandfather", one generation above your grandparents: Min oldefar var landmand (My great-grandfather was a farmer).

sentence.da: Min **oldefar** er far til min farmor.
sentence.en: My great-grandfather is the father of my grandmother.

en oldemor.explanation: "En oldemor" means "a great-grandmother", one generation above your grandparents: Min oldemor blev 98 år (My great-grandmother lived to 98).

sentence.da: Min **oldemor** er mor til min morfar.
sentence.en: My great-grandmother is the mother of my grandfather.

en oliven.explanation: "En oliven" means "an olive", a salty fruit from a tree in warm countries. The oil from it is olivenolie (olive oil): Jeg steger med olivenolie (I fry with olive oil).

sentence.da: En **oliven** er lille, grøn eller sort.
sentence.en: An olive is small, green or black.

en omkørsel.explanation: "En omkørsel" means "a detour", the route set up when a road is closed: Følg skiltene for omkørsel (Follow the signs for the detour). A longer way that you choose yourself is en omvej (a roundabout way).

sentence.da: Vi må tage en **omkørsel**, fordi vejen er lukket.
sentence.en: We have to take a detour because the road is closed.

en omvej.explanation: "En omvej" means "a detour", a longer way around: Vejen var lukket, så vi tog en omvej (The road was closed, so we took a detour). It is the opposite of en genvej (a shortcut).

sentence.da: Det er en **omvej**, fordi vejen går udenom byen.
sentence.en: It is a detour because the road goes around the town.

en onkel.explanation: "En onkel" means "an uncle". You say min onkel (my uncle), and "onkel Peter" means "Uncle Peter".

sentence.da: Min **onkel** er min fars bror.
sentence.en: My uncle is my father's brother.

en opdatering.explanation: "En opdatering" means "an update", a new version of an app or system: Telefonen venter på en opdatering (The phone is waiting for an update). The action is at opdatere (to update).

sentence.da: Min telefon skal have en **opdatering** i aften.
sentence.en: My phone needs an update tonight.

en opera.explanation: "En opera" means "an opera", and also the building where it is shown: Vi skal i operaen i aften (We are going to the opera tonight). It is different from et teater (a theater), where people mostly speak.

sentence.da: I en **opera** synger sangerne hele aftenen.
sentence.en: In an opera the singers sing all evening.

en operation.explanation: "En operation" means "an operation" or "surgery" at a hospital: Han skal have en operation i morgen (He is having an operation tomorrow). At operere means "to operate".

sentence.da: Hun skal have en **operation** på sygehuset i morgen.
sentence.en: She is having an operation at the hospital tomorrow.

en opgave.explanation: "En opgave" means "a task", at work or at school: Det er min opgave (That is my job to do). In school it can also be an exercise: en matematikopgave (a math exercise).

sentence.da: Min **opgave** er at ringe til kunderne.
sentence.en: My task is to call the customers.

en oplader.explanation: "En oplader" means "a charger" for a phone or laptop: Min oplader virker ikke (My charger does not work). The action is at oplade (to charge).

sentence.da: Jeg bruger en **oplader**, når telefonens batteri er tomt.
sentence.en: I use a charger when the phone's battery is empty.

en oplevelse.explanation: "En oplevelse" means "an experience", something you live through: Koncerten var en god oplevelse (The concert was a good experience). For work experience or skills, use erfaring (experience).

sentence.da: Turen til Italien var en stor **oplevelse**.
sentence.en: The trip to Italy was a great experience.

en oplysning.explanation: "En oplysning" means "a piece of information", one fact you are told: Kan du give mig en oplysning? (Can you give me a piece of information?) On forms, oplysninger (details) means your name, address and so on.

sentence.da: Hun gav mig en vigtig **oplysning** om prisen.
sentence.en: She gave me an important piece of information about the price.

en opskrift.explanation: "En opskrift" means "a recipe", a list of ingredients and steps for making a dish. The food comes after på (for): en opskrift på pandekager (a recipe for pancakes).

sentence.da: Jeg følger en **opskrift**, når jeg bager brød.
sentence.en: I follow a recipe when I bake bread.

en opslagstavle.explanation: "En opslagstavle" means "a bulletin board", a board where people pin notes and notices: Der hænger en seddel på opslagstavlen (There is a note on the bulletin board).

sentence.da: Jeg hængte en plakat op på en **opslagstavle**.
sentence.en: I hung a poster on a bulletin board.

en optikerforretning.explanation: "En optikerforretning" means "an optician's shop", where you buy glasses and get your eyes tested: Jeg bestiller tid i optikerforretningen (I book an appointment at the optician's).

sentence.da: Hun køber nye briller i en **optikerforretning**.
sentence.en: She buys new glasses in an optician's shop.

en opvaskebørste.explanation: "En opvaskebørste" means "a dish brush", a brush with a handle for scrubbing plates and pots: Du vasker op med opvaskebørsten (You do the dishes with the dish brush).

sentence.da: Jeg skrubber gryden med en **opvaskebørste**.
sentence.en: I scrub the pot with a dish brush.

en opvaskemaskine.explanation: "En opvaskemaskine" means "a dishwasher", the machine in a kitchen that cleans plates and cups with hot water. The person who does the job is en opvasker (a dishwasher person).

sentence.da: Vi sætter snavsede tallerkener i en **opvaskemaskine**.
sentence.en: We put dirty plates in a dishwasher.

en opvasker.explanation: "En opvasker" means "a dishwasher" when it is a person, someone who washes dishes in a restaurant: Han er opvasker i weekenden (He works as a dishwasher on the weekend). The machine is en opvaskemaskine (a dishwashing machine).

sentence.da: Som **opvasker** vasker han tallerkener hver aften.
sentence.en: As a dishwasher he washes plates every evening.

en ordbog.explanation: "En ordbog" means "a dictionary", built from ord (word) and bog (book): Hvad hedder det på engelsk? Se i ordbogen (What is it called in English? Look in the dictionary).

sentence.da: Jeg slår ordet op i en **ordbog**.
sentence.en: I look the word up in a dictionary.

en orm.explanation: "En orm" means "a worm", the long soft animal that lives in the soil. Fishermen use it as bait: Jeg har en orm på krogen (I have a worm on the hook).

sentence.da: Fuglen finder en **orm** i græsset.
sentence.en: The bird finds a worm in the grass.

en ostehandler.explanation: "En ostehandler" means "a cheesemonger", a person or shop that sells cheese: Ostehandleren har mange slags (The cheesemonger has many kinds).

sentence.da: Jeg køber ost hos en **ostehandler** i byen.
sentence.en: I buy cheese from a cheesemonger in town.

en ostemad.explanation: "En ostemad" means "a cheese sandwich", a slice of bread with cheese on it. It is ost (cheese) plus mad (food): Jeg spiser en ostemad (I eat a cheese sandwich).

sentence.da: Til frokost spiser jeg en **ostemad** og et æble.
sentence.en: For lunch I eat a cheese sandwich and an apple.

en osteskærer.explanation: "En osteskærer" means "a cheese slicer", the flat tool that cuts thin, even slices from a block of cheese: Brug osteskæreren til tynde skiver (Use the cheese slicer for thin slices).

sentence.da: Jeg skærer osten med en **osteskærer**.
sentence.en: I cut the cheese with a cheese slicer.

en overflade.explanation: "En overflade" means "a surface", the outside layer of something. It is built from over (over) and flade (flat area), and it also covers the top of water: Der er is på overfladen (There is ice on the surface).

sentence.da: Bordet har en meget glat **overflade**.
sentence.en: The table has a very smooth surface.

en overnatning.explanation: "En overnatning" means "an overnight stay", one night at a hotel or hostel: Vi har booket to overnatninger (We have booked two overnight stays). Three nights are tre overnatninger (three overnight stays).

sentence.da: Hvad koster en **overnatning** på hotellet?
sentence.en: What does an overnight stay at the hotel cost?

en overraskelse.explanation: "En overraskelse" means "a surprise", something you did not expect: Det var en stor overraskelse (It was a big surprise). To surprise someone is at overraske: Han overrasker hende med blomster (He surprises her with flowers).

sentence.da: Din gave var en dejlig **overraskelse**.
sentence.en: Your gift was a lovely surprise.

en oversigt.explanation: "En oversigt" means "an overview", a short summary that shows the main points: Her er en oversigt over ugens opgaver (Here is an overview of this week's tasks).

sentence.da: Læreren giver os en **oversigt** over kurset.
sentence.en: The teacher gives us an overview of the course.

en overskrift.explanation: "En overskrift" means "a headline", the big title above a news story: En god overskrift fanger læseren (A good headline catches the reader). It also means a heading in a document.

sentence.da: Avisen har en stor **overskrift** på forsiden.
sentence.en: The newspaper has a big headline on the front page.

en oversætter.explanation: "En oversætter" means "a translator", a person who turns written text from one language into another: Han er oversætter fra dansk til engelsk (He is a translator from Danish to English).

sentence.da: Min ven er **oversætter** og arbejder med mange sprog.
sentence.en: My friend is a translator and works with many languages.

en ovn.explanation: "En ovn" means "an oven", the one you bake and roast in. Typical phrases are i ovnen (in the oven) and at tænde ovnen (to turn on the oven). The cooking surface on top is a different word, en kogeplade (a stovetop).

sentence.da: Jeg bager en kage i en varm **ovn**.
sentence.en: I am baking a cake in a hot oven.

et offentligt toilet.explanation: "Et offentligt toilet" means "a public restroom". On signs, you may see et herretoilet (a men's restroom) or et dametoilet (a women's restroom).

forms.da: Er der et offentligt toilet her?
forms.en: Is there a public restroom here?

sentence.da: Der er et **offentligt toilet** i parken.
sentence.en: There is a public restroom in the park.

et offer.explanation: "Et offer" means "a victim", for example of a crime or an accident: Politiet talte med offeret (The police spoke with the victim). It also means "a sacrifice": Det kræver et offer (It takes a sacrifice).

sentence.da: Politiet hjalp et **offer** efter ulykken.
sentence.en: The police helped a victim after the accident.

et område.explanation: "Et område" means "an area", a part of a place: Vi bor i et roligt område (We live in a quiet area). It also means a field of knowledge: Hun er ekspert på dette område (She is an expert in this field).

sentence.da: Der er mange parker i dette **område**.
sentence.en: There are many parks in this area.

et ophold.explanation: "Et ophold" means "a stay", the time you spend somewhere, such as in a hotel. It also fits a short stop on a trip: et kort ophold (a short stop).

sentence.da: Vi havde et dejligt **ophold** på hotellet.
sentence.en: We had a lovely stay at the hotel.

et opkald.explanation: "Et opkald" means "a phone call", seen from the phone: Jeg har et opkald fra min chef (I have a call from my boss). A friendly chat on the phone is often en samtale (a conversation).

sentence.da: Jeg fik et **opkald** fra skolen i dag.
sentence.en: I got a call from the school today.

et opslag.explanation: "Et opslag" means "a post" on social media: Hun skrev et opslag om sin ferie (She wrote a post about her vacation). It also means a notice on a board, like et opslag på skolen (a notice at the school).

sentence.da: Hun delte et **opslag** om sin nye bog.
sentence.en: She shared a post about her new book.

et ord.explanation: "Et ord" means "a word". Hvad betyder det ord? means "What does that word mean?". A dictionary is en ordbog, literally a word book.

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke finde det **ord** i ordbogen.
sentence.en: I cannot find that word in the dictionary.

offentlig.explanation: "Offentlig" means "public" and describes things that belong to everyone, such as the state or the town: et offentligt bibliotek (a public library). The opposite is privat (private).

sentence.da: En **offentlig** skole er gratis for alle.
sentence.en: A public school is free for everyone.

officiel.explanation: "Officiel" means "official", for what comes from the government or another authority: Det er officielt (It is official).

sentence.da: Det er en **officiel** meddelelse fra kommunen.
sentence.en: It is an official notice from the municipality.

offline.explanation: "Offline" means "offline", not connected to the internet: Appen virker offline (The app works offline). Det er et offline spil (It is an offline game).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke søge, fordi min telefon er **offline**.
sentence.en: I cannot search because my phone is offline.

ofte.explanation: "Ofte" means "often". Compare Jeg går ofte i skoven (I often walk in the forest) with Jeg går aldrig i skoven (I never walk in the forest). To ask, say Hvor ofte træner du? (How often do you work out?).

sentence.da: Vi spiser **ofte** ude.
sentence.en: We often eat out.

oftest.explanation: "Oftest" means "most often" and describes what happens in most cases: Jeg spiser oftest hjemme (I most often eat at home). It comes from ofte (often): ofte, oftere (more often), oftest.

forms.en: It most often happens in the evening

sentence.da: Jeg tager **oftest** bussen.
sentence.en: I most often take the bus.

og.explanation: "Og" means "and": Jeg har en bror og en søster (I have a brother and a sister). Do not mix it up with også (also, too): Jeg kan også lide te (I also like tea). Og sounds like a short o, with no g sound.

sentence.da: Jeg kan lide kaffe **og** te.
sentence.en: I like coffee and tea.

også.explanation: "Også" means "also" or "too". Compare Jeg kommer også (I am coming too) with Jeg kommer heller ikke (I am not coming either). Do not mix it up with og (and): te og kaffe (tea and coffee).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **også** have kaffe.
sentence.en: I also want coffee.

okay.explanation: "Okay" means "okay", the same word as in English. You use it to agree or to show you understand.

sentence.da: Vi ses klokken fem. – **Okay**!
sentence.en: See you at five. – Okay!

okay så.explanation: "Okay så" means "okay then" and accepts what was said, or starts the next step: Okay så, vi gør det (Okay then, we'll do it). It is casual and friendly.

sentence.da: **Okay så**, vi mødes klokken otte.
sentence.en: Okay then, we'll meet at eight.

oksekød.explanation: "Oksekød" means "beef". It is made from okse (ox) and kød (meat), so it is literally ox meat. Kød on its own means any kind of meat.

sentence.da: Burgeren er lavet af **oksekød**.
sentence.en: The burger is made of beef.

oktober.explanation: "Oktober" means "October". Danish spells it with a k, where English has a c. Like all month names, it is written with a small letter.

sentence.da: Efter september kommer **oktober**.
sentence.en: After September comes October.

olie.explanation: "Olie" means "oil". Put the kind in front to name it: rapsolie (rapeseed oil), olivenolie (olive oil).

sentence.da: Jeg steger kødet i **olie**.
sentence.en: I fry the meat in oil.

olivenolie.explanation: "Olivenolie" means "olive oil", built from oliven (olive) and olie (oil). Use it for salad or frying: Jeg bruger olivenolie i salaten (I use olive oil in the salad).

sentence.da: Jeg steger fisken i **olivenolie**.
sentence.en: I fry the fish in olive oil.

om.explanation: "Om" means "about", in (time from now) or "if". En bog om Danmark means "a book about Denmark". Om en uge means "in a week", unlike i en uge (for a week). And "Jeg ved ikke, om han kommer" means "I do not know if he is coming".

sentence.da: Filmen starter **om** en time.
sentence.en: The film starts in an hour.

om aftenen.explanation: "Om aftenen" means "in the evening", for something you do again and again. Compare Jeg læser om aftenen (I read in the evening, every evening) with Jeg læser i aften (I will read this evening, just today).

forms.en: In the evening we watch TV.
What do you do in the evening?

sentence.da: Vi ser tv **om aftenen**.
sentence.en: We watch TV in the evening.

om lidt.explanation: "Om lidt" means "in a little while" or "soon". Compare Jeg kommer nu (I am coming now) with Jeg kommer om lidt (I am coming in a little while).

forms.en: I am coming in a little while.
See you in a little while.

sentence.da: Maden er klar **om lidt**.
sentence.en: The food will be ready in a little while.

om morgenen.explanation: "Om morgenen" means "in the morning", for something you do again and again. Compare Jeg drikker kaffe om morgenen (I drink coffee in the morning, every morning) with Jeg drak kaffe i morges (I drank coffee this morning, just today).

forms.en: I get up in the morning.
In the morning I drink coffee.

sentence.da: Jeg står op klokken seks **om morgenen**.
sentence.en: I get up at six in the morning.

om natten.explanation: "Om natten" means "at night", for something that happens every night. Compare Jeg sover om natten (I sleep at night) with Jeg sov dårligt i nat (I slept badly last night).

sentence.da: Alle sover **om natten**.
sentence.en: Everyone sleeps at night.

om ugen.explanation: "Om ugen" means "per week" and tells how often something happens. The same pattern works for other times: to gange om dagen (twice a day), fem dage om ugen (five days a week).

forms.da: Jeg arbejder fem dage om ugen.
forms.en: I work five days a week.

sentence.da: Jeg træner tre gange **om ugen**.
sentence.en: I work out three times a week.

om året.explanation: "Om året" means "per year" and tells how often something happens: Jeg rejser tre gange om året (I travel three times a year). The same pattern works for a week: to gange om ugen (twice a week).

forms.da: Vi ses fire gange om året
forms.en: We see each other four times a year

sentence.da: Jeg besøger min mor to gange **om året**.
sentence.en: I visit my mother twice a year.

ombord.explanation: "Ombord" means "on board" a ship, plane or train: Hun går ombord på færgen (She goes on board the ferry). The opposite is i land (ashore): Vi går i land (We go ashore).

sentence.da: Alle er nu **ombord**, og færgen sejler.
sentence.en: Everyone is now on board and the ferry sails.

omkring.explanation: "Omkring" means "around". It works for a place: Vi går omkring søen (We walk around the lake). It also works for a rough number or time: omkring tyve mennesker (about twenty people), omkring klokken otte (around eight o'clock).

sentence.da: Der er mange træer **omkring** huset.
sentence.en: There are many trees around the house.

ond.explanation: "Ond" means "evil" or "wicked": en ond konge (an evil king). It also means "painful" in set phrases: Det gør ondt (It hurts) and Jeg har ondt i hovedet (I have a headache).

sentence.da: Heksen i historien er meget **ond**.
sentence.en: The witch in the story is very evil.

ondt.explanation: "Ondt" means "pain" or "hurt". Danish says Jeg har ondt i maven, literally I have pain in the stomach, where English says my stomach hurts. Do not say Jeg er ondt (I am pain).

sentence.da: Jeg har **ondt** i maven.
sentence.en: My stomach hurts.

online.explanation: "Online" means "online", connected to the internet. It is spelled the same as in English and never changes: en online butik (an online store), et online kursus (an online course).

sentence.da: Man kan købe bøger **online**.
sentence.en: You can buy books online.

onsdag.explanation: "Onsdag" means "Wednesday". Like all day names, it starts with a small letter. Use på onsdag (on Wednesday, coming up) for the next one, and om onsdagen (on Wednesdays) for every week.

sentence.da: Efter tirsdag kommer **onsdag**.
sentence.en: After Tuesday comes Wednesday.

op.explanation: "Op" means "up", for moving up. Compare Kom op! (Come up!) with Han er oppe på loftet (He is up in the attic): oppe is for being there. It is also part of at stå op (to get up out of bed).

sentence.da: Katten hopper **op** på bordet.
sentence.en: The cat jumps up onto the table.

opdateret.explanation: "Opdateret" means "updated", with the newest information or version: Er listen opdateret? (Is the list up to date?) It also fits a person who knows the latest news.

sentence.da: Min telefon er **opdateret** og virker nu fint.
sentence.en: My phone is updated and now works fine.

opførsel.explanation: "Opførsel" means "behavior", how a person acts around others: Hans opførsel var ikke i orden (His behavior was not okay). Pæn opførsel means "good manners".

sentence.da: Hans **opførsel** over for børnene var meget pæn.
sentence.en: His behavior toward the children was very nice.

opladning.explanation: "Opladning" means "charging", giving a battery power again: Opladningen tager en time (The charging takes an hour). The action is at oplade (to charge).

sentence.da: Min telefon er på **opladning** lige nu.
sentence.en: My phone is charging right now.

opmærksom.explanation: "Opmærksom" means "attentive" or "aware": Vær opmærksom! (Pay attention!) With på (on) it means aware of something: Jeg er opmærksom på problemet (I am aware of the problem).

sentence.da: Min datter er **opmærksom** og lytter godt.
sentence.en: My daughter is attentive and listens well.

opmærksomhed.explanation: "Opmærksomhed" means "attention", the focus you give to someone or something: Hun fik meget opmærksomhed (She got a lot of attention). To pay attention, say at være opmærksom (to be attentive).

sentence.da: Babyen græder for at få **opmærksomhed**.
sentence.en: The baby cries to get attention.

oppe.explanation: "Oppe" means "up there", for where something is. Compare Katten hopper op på bordet (The cat jumps up onto the table) with Katten er oppe på bordet (The cat is up on the table). Er du oppe? (Are you up?) asks whether someone is out of bed.

sentence.da: Bogen ligger **oppe** på hylden.
sentence.en: The book is up on the shelf.

optaget.explanation: "Optaget" means "busy", taken or "occupied". Use it for a phone line, a toilet, a seat, or a person who has no time. Er her optaget? (Is this taken?) asks whether a seat is taken.

sentence.da: Toilettet er **optaget** lige nu.
sentence.en: The toilet is occupied right now.

optimistisk.explanation: "Optimistisk" means "optimistic" and describes someone who expects things to go well: Jeg er optimistisk om fremtiden (I am optimistic about the future). The opposite is pessimistisk (pessimistic).

sentence.da: Hun er **optimistisk** og tror altid på det bedste.
sentence.en: She is optimistic and always believes in the best.

opvaskemiddel.explanation: "Opvaskemiddel" means "dish soap": Jeg bruger opvaskemiddel til glas og kopper (I use dish soap on glasses and cups). It is not for clothes; for those you use vaskepulver (laundry detergent).

sentence.da: Jeg bruger **opvaskemiddel**, når jeg vasker op.
sentence.en: I use dish soap when I wash dishes.

orange.explanation: "Orange" means "orange", the color. For the fruit, Danes say en appelsin (an orange), not orange. The color word never changes, whatever it describes: en orange bil (an orange car), orange biler (orange cars).

sentence.da: Gulerødder er **orange**.
sentence.en: Carrots are orange.

ordentlig.explanation: "Ordentlig" means "proper" or "decent", done well and as it should be: Jeg vil have en ordentlig middag (I want a proper dinner). For a person it means well-behaved: en ordentlig mand (a decent man).

sentence.da: Du skal have **ordentlig** mad, ikke bare chips.
sentence.en: You must have proper food, not just chips.

organiseret.explanation: "Organiseret" means "organized", with everything in order and planned: Hun er altid organiseret (She is always organized). Velorganiseret (well organized) is also common.

sentence.da: Hun er **organiseret** og kommer aldrig for sent.
sentence.en: She is organized and never comes late.

original.explanation: "Original" means "original": the first real one, not a copy. It can also mean "creative and new": en original idé (an original idea).

sentence.da: Det er en **original** tegning, ikke en kopi.
sentence.en: It is an original drawing, not a copy.

os.explanation: "Os" means "us". Compare Vi ser ham (We see him) with Han ser os (He sees us): vi is we, os is us. It is also used after words like med (with): Kom med os! (Come with us!).

related.en: you (more than one, after words like "med")

sentence.da: Vil du komme med **os**?
sentence.en: Do you want to come with us?

ost.explanation: "Ost" means "cheese". When you mean one kind of cheese, say en ost: en fransk ost means "a French cheese". Without en it is cheese in general.

sentence.da: **Ost** er lavet af mælk.
sentence.en: Cheese is made from milk.

otte.explanation: "Otte" means "eight". Do not mix it up with atten (eighteen): otte børn (eight children) but atten børn (eighteen children).

sentence.da: Efter syv kommer **otte**.
sentence.en: After seven comes eight.

ottende.explanation: "Ottende" means "eighth": den ottende dag (the eighth day). It is also used for dates: den ottende marts (the eighth of March).

sentence.da: Efter den syvende dag kommer den **ottende** dag.
sentence.en: After the seventh day comes the eighth day.

ovenpå.explanation: "Ovenpå" means "upstairs", on the floor above you. It works for where something is and for going there: Jeg bor ovenpå (I live upstairs), Jeg går ovenpå (I go upstairs). The opposite is nedenunder (downstairs).

sentence.da: Soveværelset er **ovenpå**, og køkkenet er nede.
sentence.en: The bedroom is upstairs, and the kitchen is down.

over.explanation: "Over" means "over", above or "across". Compare Lampen hænger over bordet (The lamp hangs above the table) with Han går over gaden (He walks across the street). With amounts it means "more than": over to timer (more than two hours).

sentence.da: Lampen hænger **over** bordet.
sentence.en: The lamp hangs over the table.

overalt.explanation: "Overalt" means "everywhere", in every place. It can also start a sentence for emphasis: Overalt er der blomster (Everywhere there are flowers). The opposite is ingen steder (nowhere).

sentence.da: Jeg leder **overalt** efter nøglen.
sentence.en: I look everywhere for the key.

overfor.explanation: "Overfor" means "opposite" or "across from": Banken ligger overfor skolen (The bank is across from the school). It can also mean "facing": Jeg står overfor et valg (I am facing a choice).

sentence.da: Min ven bor **overfor** biblioteket.
sentence.en: My friend lives across from the library.

overhovedet.explanation: "Overhovedet" means "at all" and is used with ikke (not) or in questions: Jeg forstår overhovedet ikke (I do not understand at all).

forms.en: It is not difficult at all.

sentence.da: Jeg har **overhovedet** ikke tid i dag.
sentence.en: I have no time at all today.

overraskende.explanation: "Overraskende" means "surprising" and describes news or events that you did not expect: Det er overraskende nyt (That is surprising news). To say how you feel, use overrasket: Jeg er overrasket (I am surprised).

sentence.da: Resultatet var **overraskende**.
sentence.en: The result was surprising.

overskyet.explanation: "Overskyet" means "overcast", with the whole sky covered by clouds. It is stronger than skyet (cloudy), which can mean just a few clouds.

sentence.da: Himlen er **overskyet** i dag.
sentence.en: The sky is overcast today.
